notes: Clean course, dominated by false positives: ~86% are component sub-glosses of agglutinative verb stems/postpositions (करना, कि, नहीं, से) or pure English inflection/article/contraction of one lemma (I/I'm/I'll, word/words, friend/friends, the answer/an answer). The real fixes cluster in two systemic patterns: (1) the SSi literal-order 'build' row vs natural-order 'use' row of the same sentence (consolidate to natural English), and (2) genuine Hindi ambiguities surfacing as overloaded prompts — बहुत (very/too), वह (he/she), and कल (yesterday/tomorrow). No high-frequency drilled token is overloaded, so nothing is release-blocking.

real_fixes.action: Re-gloss the bare 'Sunday morning' build row to 'on Sunday morning' so the time-phrase prompt maps 1:1.

real_fixes.known: मुझे आश्चर्य है कि यह ज़रूरी है।
targets: I wonder if this is important
real_fixes.action: यह = this/it; consolidate the build twin to 'it's important' to match the use form.
बहुत = very/a lot, not 'too' (excessive). 'too busy' overloads the LEGO; either re-gloss to 'very busy' or change the Hindi to बहुत ज़्यादा व्यस्त for the 'too busy' sense.
Same बहुत = very/too overload at sentence level (downstream of बहुत व्यस्त); align to 'very busy today' or differentiate the Hindi for the 'too busy' reading.

targets: will you be ready to go?
real_fixes.action: Two genuinely different drilled renderings of one prompt: a question vs a statement, and go vs leave (जाना). Differentiate the Hindi (e.g. interrogation marker / जाना vs निकलना) so each maps 1:1.
वह is gender-neutral 3rd-person; same prompt yields he and she. Inherent Hindi ambiguity overloads the prompt — either accept both as valid answers or supply disambiguating context.
कल = yesterday OR tomorrow; कल रात is genuinely ambiguous (last night vs tomorrow night), both drilled. Differentiate via बीती रात (last night) vs कल रात (tomorrow night) or context.
रात को = 'at night'; the 'very well' gloss (seed 55 component) is a data error with no path from the Hindi. Correct that single row.
एक विचार = 'an idea'; the 'that's a idea' gloss is ungrammatical ('a idea') and adds 'that's'. Fix that single component row to 'an idea'.
